highlights: Ordinance 2025-25, creating a separate vehicle replacement fund for the stormwater utility, was approved.
The Town Council voted to formally explore a proposal to reorganize and merge with Richland Township.
An amendment passed requiring all meetings pertaining to the proposed Ellettsville-Richland Township reorganization to be public.
transcriptSummary.prose: The Ellettsville Town Council meeting on November 10th, 2025, began with standard procedures including a prayer, the Pledge of Allegiance, and roll call. The minutes from the October 27th, 2025 meeting were approved, as were accounts payable and payroll vouchers. The council then moved to Ordinance 2025-25, which creates a separate non-reverting vehicle replacement fund for the stormwater utility, to be funded by a portion of utility rates. This ordinance was approved following a roll call vote. New business included an announcement for the "Santa on Sail Street" event scheduled for December 13th, 2025. A significant portion of the meeting was dedicated to discussing a proposal to explore reorganizing Ellettsville into a single government entity with Richland Township. It was emphasized that this is an exploratory step, not an annexation, aimed at proactively addressing state-level pressures on rural townships, preserving local identity, and improving efficiency and sustainability. The process would involve a reorganization committee, subcommittees, and a public referendum in November 2026, with an effective date of January 1st, 2027. A motion was made to proceed with this exploration. An amendment was introduced and approved, stipulating that all meetings related to the reorganization would be public, before the primary motion to explore the reorganization was also approved by a unanimous roll call vote. The Town Manager recognized the police, fire, and DPW departments for their efficient repair of a 12-inch water main during a recent Friday night outage. Supervisor comments were brief, with the Deputy Fire Chief mentioning a lack of donors for a department calendar. Council comments included congratulations to the Ellettsville Marching Mustangs for their state championship and reiterated the historic significance of the reorganization exploration, encouraging public involvement and emphasizing transparency and mutual benefit for both the town and the township. The meeting then adjourned.

highlights: Approved Accounts Payable Vouchers and Payroll.
Approved Ordinance 2025-25 establishing a separate Vehicle Replacement Fund for the Stormwater Utility.
Voted to initiate the process to explore consolidation with Richland Township, including a commitment for all related meetings to be public.
documentsSummary.prose: The Ellettsville Town Council convened for a special meeting on November 10, 2025. All council members were present. The council approved the minutes from their October 27, 2025, regular meeting, followed by the approval of Accounts Payable Vouchers and Payroll. A key decision was the unanimous approval of Ordinance 2025-25, which creates a non-reverting Vehicle Replacement Fund specifically for the Stormwater Utility, to be financed by a portion of stormwater fees. Town Manager Michael Farmer announced details for the upcoming 'Santa on Sale Street' event on December 13th. The main discussion focused on exploring a proposed consolidation with Richland Township. This initiative is a response to recent changes in state tax laws and potential state-level discussions about eliminating township governments, aiming to protect essential services and ensure sustainable growth. The proposed process involves forming committees, developing a reorganization plan for approval by both the Township Advisory Board and the Town Council, and a public referendum in November 2026, with an effective date of January 1, 2027. The council voted to enter into an agreement to examine the facts for reorganization and establish committees, with an amendment stipulating that all meetings related to the consolidation efforts will be public. The meeting concluded after brief comments from supervisors and council members.
